title: Promptster: Analyzing Engineers' AI Coding Tool Usage
description: Project featured in Hacker News 'Ask HN: What Are You Working On?' that analyzes engineers' work with AI coding tools including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Copilot. The project aims to understand usage patterns and effectiveness of different AI coding assistants.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Summer AI Developer Program: Is Learning to Code DEAD in 2026?
description: Educational program scheduled for July 13-24, 2026, focusing on AI developer tools including ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor AI. The program addresses the fundamental question of whether traditional coding skills remain relevant in an era of advanced AI coding assistants, and how developers should adapt their skill sets.
author: AI Developer Education Program

title: How To Do Feature Engineering with AI
description: Two Minute Papers video from July 12, 2026, covering feature engineering and converting data into audience insights using AI tools in 2026.
author: Two Minute Papers (Károly Zsolnai-Fehér)

title: The 2026 State of AI Coding Report
description: New Relic's comprehensive report on AI coding in 2026. Key findings include how AI-generated code is speeding development but complicating production environments. The report covers adoption rates, productivity impacts, code quality considerations, and best practices for integrating AI coding tools into professional workflows.
author: New Relic

title: Best AI Coding Tools for Developers in 2026
description: Fireship video exploring the top AI coding tools of 2026, comprehensive guide for developers on AI-assisted development.
author: Fireship

title: AI Coding Agents in 2026: A Practical Roadmap
description: As of July 2026, AI coding tools have evolved from simple autocomplete to engineered agent workflows. This guide provides practical insights into implementing multi-agent systems, prompt engineering for code generation, and best practices for integrating AI agents into development pipelines.
author: CodePick.dev

title: Why Write Code in 2026
description: Hacker News discussion about the role of human programmers in 2026. Covers LLMs undergoing reinforcement learning on coding, challenges with assembly generation and token inefficiency, and how AI is changing systems thinking and auditing practices.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Best AI Coding Tools July 2026: Post-GPT-5.6 Rankings
description: Comprehensive ranking of AI coding tools following the release of GPT-5.6. Claude Code emerges as the top choice, with Cursor holding the #2 IDE spot after the Cursor 3 rebuild. OpenCode is listed as the most practical free option. The analysis reflects the rapidly evolving landscape of AI-assisted development tools.
author: Agensi.io

title: The new GPT-5.6 family: Luna, Terra, Sol
description: OpenAI's latest flagship model hit general availability on July 9, 2026, coming in three sizes: Luna, Terra, and Sol (from smallest to largest). Simon Willison provides analysis of the new model family and its implications for AI development.
author: Simon Willison

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Comprehensive 4.5-hour discussion with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka covering the current state of AI technology. Topics include closed vs open LLMs, programming & dev tooling, scaling laws, China's role in AI, AI agents, GPU developments, and paths to AGI. The episode provides deep insights into how AI is reshaping software development and the broader technology landscape.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Best AI Coding Agents (July 2026): Scored Leaderboard
description: Comprehensive benchmarking and leaderboard of AI coding agents. Codex CLI on GPT-5.5 leads Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 83.4% accuracy. The report provides detailed performance analysis across different coding tasks and benchmarks, reflecting the maturation of AI coding agent capabilities.
author: MorphLLM

title: Rewriting Bun in Rust: A Case Study in Agentic Engineering
description: Jarred Sumner's detailed blog post about rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust using AI coding agents. The project used coordinated parallel agents and a conformance suite to automate the port. The rewrite took 11 days and consumed an estimated $165,000 in tokens, demonstrating how AI agents enable ambitious projects that were previously considered impractical.
author: Simon Willison (covering Jarred Sumner)

title: Introducing GPT-Live: OpenAI's Voice Mode Upgrade
description: OpenAI upgraded the model used by ChatGPT voice mode to a frontier model with ability to delegate harder tasks to GPT-5.5. Simon Willison reports on the improved capabilities and practical experiences during the preview period, including the model's ability to maintain conversation flow while handling complex background tasks.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI-Written Change Descriptions: A Moratorium
description: Kenton Varda declared a moratorium against AI-written change descriptions (PR and commit messages, issues/tickets) from his team. The insight: AI was writing worse-than-useful descriptions that outlined code details visible in the code itself while omitting the higher-level framing needed to understand what the code is doing.
author: Kenton Varda (via Simon Willison)

title: How I Write Software with LLMs
description: Hacker News discussion exploring style differences between LLM and human-generated code, covering code density differences between AI and human developers and practical workflows.
author: Hacker News Community

title: sqlite-utils 4.0: Now with Database Schema Migrations
description: Simon Willison released sqlite-utils 4.0, the 124th release of the project and first major version bump since 2020. This version introduces database migrations, nested transactions via db.atomic(), and support for compound foreign keys. The release was heavily assisted by Claude Fable AI coding agent.
author: Simon Willison
